governanceNotes: D1 batch 79 (2026-09-27): two bounded association edges authored - rhinitis-vasomotor to asthma (rank 1) and rhinitis-vasomotor to migraine-headaches (rank 2) - both classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The edges rest on disjoint sources this batch (deliberately no within-batch shared-source provenance while the CRG redundancy-semantics question stands at eleven accumulated examples): the asthma edge on the Copenhagen birth-cohort comparison (non-allergic rhinitis asthma prevalence 20 percent versus 5 percent in controls, matching the allergic group at 21 percent, PMID 20816191), the 2024 upper-airway-comorbidity review (PMID 39426424), and the 2024 non-allergic-rhinopathy comprehensive review (PMID 38467330); the migraine-headaches edge on the 2026 prospective clinical study (migraine in 22.9 percent of the non-allergic subgroup versus 16.0 percent of controls under ICHD-3, PMID 41605462), the American Migraine Prevalence and Prevention population study (66.8 percent of migraine cases with rhinitis; adjusted OR 1.25 for any rhinitis on headache frequency, PMID 24275145), and the dedicated vasomotor-rhinitis and migraine report (PMID 33713559, registered for title-level association only because the PubMed record carries no abstract). Null-anchor discipline is applied visibly: the asthma cohort's finding that bronchial hyperresponsiveness and exhaled nitric oxide elevation were confined to the allergic subgroup is carried openly as a counterweight to the airway-hyperresponsiveness mechanism, and the population migraine anchor's MIDAS disability null (OR 1.10, 95 percent CI 0.96-1.26) is carried openly alongside its positive frequency result. The mixed-rhinitis stratum, not the non-allergic stratum, carries the population anchor's fully adjusted significance and is named as such. Constitutive-proximity cleared: nasal obstruction is not a diagnostic criterion of either target. The sinusitis, chronic-sinusitis, allergic-rhinitis, sleep-apnea, and insomnia propositions are withheld on the record with reasons, and the anosmia gap is recorded as a catalog-gap continuation with no authoring-quality cohort located.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Non-allergic (vasomotor) rhinitis associates with asthma at population level, and the located cohort separates that association from an allergic one: the Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood analysis of 38 seven-year-old children with allergic rhinitis, 67 with non-allergic rhinitis, and 185 without rhinitis found children with non-allergic rhinitis had increased asthma prevalence of 20 percent versus 5 percent in controls (P=0.001), the same magnitude as the allergic-rhinitis group at 21 percent (P=0.002), while non-allergic rhinitis showed no association with filaggrin null mutations, eczema, food sensitisation, total IgE, blood eosinophil count, fractional exhaled nitric oxide, or bronchial hyperresponsiveness - leading the authors to conclude that asthma is similarly associated with allergic and non-allergic rhinitis, suggesting a link between upper and lower airways beyond allergy-associated inflammation (PMID 20816191); the 2024 review of upper-airway comorbidities of asthma frames allergic or non-allergic rhinitis, chronic rhinosinusitis with or without nasal polyps, and aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease as upper-airway comorbidities closely related to asthma phenotypes under the one-airway one-disease concept (PMID 39426424); and the 2024 comprehensive review of non-allergic rhinopathy lists asthma among the comorbidities associated with non-allergic rhinitis alongside rhinosinusitis, headaches, chronic cough, and sleep disturbances, and stresses that accurate diagnosis matters because inappropriate therapies lead to poor clinical outcomes (PMID 38467330); recorded as documented association only with the anchor limits carried openly - the cohort is children, the two reviews describe framework rather than quantify, and the cohort's own finding that non-allergic rhinitis carried no bronchial hyperresponsiveness is a material internal counterweight that limits any lower-airway mechanistic inference.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of asthma is established for any individual: the located cohort is cross-sectional with 67 exposed children and measures co-occurrence at one age rather than incidence, the same cohort reports that non-allergic rhinitis was NOT associated with bronchial hyperresponsiveness or elevated exhaled nitric oxide, and so the airway-hyperresponsiveness mechanism the one-airway framework implies is not demonstrated in the non-allergic subgroup, while the reverse direction (asthma treated with drugs affecting the nose, or asthma itself producing rhinitis symptoms) is equally consistent with the cross-sectional design; individual claims require dated asthma diagnosis with objective obstruction or variability testing, dated non-allergic rhinitis diagnosis with negative aeroallergen and IgE workup, and exclusion of allergic rhinitis, chronic rhinosinusitis, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease, and drug effects.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Nasal mucosal sensory and autonomic dysfunction in non-allergic rhinitis - the neurogenic reflex arc the capsaicin/TRPV1 literature describes as hypersensitive sensory afferents releasing neuropeptides into the nasal mucosa - is hypothesized to influence lower-airway tone and bronchial responsiveness in the same individual, the route the one-airway framework and the co-occurrence cohort support, but whether the nasal condition produced any individual's asthma remains hypothesized and the located cohort's null bronchial-hyperresponsiveness finding for the non-allergic subgroup actively limits the route.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at birth-cohort and double-review class following the upper-airway comorbidity convention (the registered allergic-rhinitis, nasal-polyps, atopic-dermatitis-eczema, bronchiolitis, gerd, churg-strauss-syndrome, and eosinophilic-bronchitis to asthma edges): the birth-cohort anchor is the only located design with exposed and unexposed denominators and it reports a non-allergic-rhinitis asthma prevalence of 20 percent versus 5 percent in controls with the same pattern as the allergic group (PMID 20816191), the upper-airway-comorbidity review supplies the current framework under which the association is maintained as one-airway one-disease (PMID 39426424), and the non-allergic-rhinopathy review supplies the subtype-specific framing and the diagnostic-accuracy caution (PMID 38467330); because the cohort is cross-sectional, paediatric, and reports the mechanism's own proximal marker (bronchial hyperresponsiveness) as absent in the non-allergic subgroup, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with that null carried openly and routes individual claims through a confirmed asthma diagnosis with objective testing and the allergic and medication-driven alternatives excluded.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The only located cohort is cross-sectional with 67 exposed children and cannot establish temporal direction between the two conditions; that cohort reports bronchial hyperresponsiveness and elevated exhaled nitric oxide as present only in the allergic group, so the proximal lower-airway mechanism is not demonstrated in the non-allergic subgroup; no located anchor separates non-allergic rhinitis from the mixed and unclassified subtypes quantitatively in an asthma outcome; no located cohort reports incident asthma after a confirmed non-allergic rhinitis diagnosis in adults; a separate 2013 pediatric methacholine-challenge study found bronchial hyperresponsiveness in only 25.5 percent of children with non-allergic rhinitis against 55.7 percent with allergic rhinitis and reported that persistent rhinitis symptoms did not increase hyperresponsiveness risk in the non-allergic group (PMID 23710946), which is carried here as a second counterweight to the airway-hyperresponsiveness mechanism though it is not among this edge's three registered references
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Allergic rhinitis or mixed rhinitis misclassified as non-allergic rhinitis, which the classification review flags as a recognised confounder
Aspirin or NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease with nasal polyps, an alternative upper-airway route to asthma
Intranasal corticosteroid, antihistamine, or decongestant treatment effects on lower-airway outcomes
Chronic rhinosinusitis, the coexisting upper-airway identity the non-allergic rhinopathy review lists separately

evidenceGaps: The only located cohort is cross-sectional with 67 exposed children and cannot establish temporal direction between the two conditions; that cohort reports bronchial hyperresponsiveness and elevated exhaled nitric oxide as present only in the allergic group, so the proximal lower-airway mechanism is not demonstrated in the non-allergic subgroup; no located anchor separates non-allergic rhinitis from the mixed and unclassified subtypes quantitatively in an asthma outcome; no located cohort reports incident asthma after a confirmed non-allergic rhinitis diagnosis in adults; a separate 2013 pediatric methacholine-challenge study found bronchial hyperresponsiveness in only 25.5 percent of children with non-allergic rhinitis against 55.7 percent with allergic rhinitis and reported that persistent rhinitis symptoms did not increase hyperresponsiveness risk in the non-allergic group (PMID 23710946), which is carried here as a second counterweight to the airway-hyperresponsiveness mechanism though it is not among this edge's three registered references
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the population-level co-occurrence is quantified with unexposed denominators in a prospective birth cohort, matching the allergic-rhinitis magnitude, and because two current reviews maintain the upper-airway framework; the conservative framing carries the cohort's own null proximal finding openly, so the association is visible while the mechanistic route and any direction remain explicitly unasserted.

sourceReferences.citation: Chawes BL, Bønnelykke K, Kreiner-Møller E, et al. Children with allergic and nonallergic rhinitis have a similar risk of asthma J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2010 Sep;126(3):567-73.e1-8. PMID 20816191.
sourceReferences.note: Birth-cohort comparison of 38 children with allergic rhinitis, 67 with non-allergic rhinitis, and 185 controls finding asthma prevalence of 21, 20, and 5 percent respectively, with no association of non-allergic rhinitis with IgE, eosinophils, exhaled nitric oxide, filaggrin mutations, or bronchial hyperresponsiveness.

sourceReferences.citation: Jung CG, Buchheit KM, Bochenek G, et al. Upper airway comorbidities of asthma J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2024 Dec;154(6):1343-1354. PMID 39426424.
sourceReferences.note: Review of upper-airway comorbidities of asthma framing allergic or non-allergic rhinitis, chronic rhinosinusitis with or without polyps, and aspirin/NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease as comorbidities affecting asthma phenotypes.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2024;154(6):1343-1354. Narrative review; abstract states upper-airway comorbidities are closely related to asthma phenotypes under the one-airway one-disease concept and influence management and biologic selection.

sourceReferences.citation: Baroody FM, Gevaert P, Smith PK, et al. Nonallergic Rhinopathy: A Comprehensive Review of Classification, Diagnosis, and Treatment J Allergy Clin Immunol Pract. 2024 Jun;12(6):1436-1447. PMID 38467330.
sourceReferences.note: Comprehensive review of non-allergic rhinopathy listing rhinosinusitis, headaches, asthma, chronic cough, and sleep disturbances as associated comorbidities and stressing accurate subtype diagnosis.

Comprehensive review; abstract states comorbidities associated with NAR include rhinosinusitis, headaches, asthma, chronic cough, and sleep disturbances, and that inaccurate diagnosis leads to inappropriate therapy.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Non-allergic (vasomotor) rhinitis associates with migraine at clinic and population level: the 2026 prospective cross-sectional clinical study of 497 participants (200 allergic rhinitis, 109 non-allergic rhinitis, 188 controls) with neurologist ICHD-3 assessment found migraine prevalence of 24.9 percent in the combined rhinitis group versus 16.0 percent in controls (OR 1.75, P=0.018), with the non-allergic group at 22.9 percent and the allergic group highest at 26.0 percent, and both rhinitis groups scoring significantly worse on Total Rhinoconjunctivitis Score and Nasal Obstruction Symptom Evaluation than controls (P<0.001) (PMID 41605462); the American Migraine Prevalence and Prevention longitudinal study of 5,849 people with migraine found 66.8 percent had rhinitis with mixed rhinitis the most common form, and that the presence of rhinitis of any type was associated with headache frequency in the fully adjusted model (OR 1.25, 95 percent CI 1.05-1.49), with mixed rhinitis associated with an increased headache-frequency category after adjustment for all covariates (OR 1.28, 95 percent CI 1.05-1.57) (PMID 24275145); and the 2021 report directly examining the pair states its finding as an association between migraine and vasomotor rhinitis in a dedicated cohort of patients presenting to an otorhinolaryngology service (PMID 33713559); recorded as documented association only with the anchor limits carried openly - the subtype-specific quantitative anchor is cross-sectional, the population anchor reports rhinitis subtypes in aggregate and its mixed-rhinitis stratum dominates the significant result, the dedicated vasomotor-rhinitis anchor carries no abstract and is registered for the title-level association only, and the population anchor's own headache-disability measure (MIDAS) lost significance in the fully adjusted model (OR 1.10, 95 percent CI 0.96-1.26).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of migraine is established for any individual: the subtype-specific anchor is cross-sectional, the population anchor is conditioned on the migraine sample so it cannot establish which condition preceded the other, the mixed-rhinitis stratum rather than the non-allergic stratum carries the fully adjusted significance, the same anchor's disability outcome went null after full adjustment, and medication over-use is an obvious unmeasured cofactor since rhinitis patients self-medicate with analgesics; individual claims require dated migraine diagnosis with ICHD criteria, dated non-allergic rhinitis diagnosis with negative aeroallergen workup, and exclusion of analgesic or NSAID over-use headache, allergic rhinitis, and medication effects.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Neurogenic inflammation of the nasal mucosa in non-allergic rhinitis - sensory-afferent activation with local neuropeptide release including calcitonin gene-related peptide pathways, the route the capsaicin/TRPV1 mechanism describes - is hypothesized to sensitise trigeminal nociceptive signalling so that headache-prone individuals experience migraine at higher frequency, but whether the nasal condition produced any individual's migraine remains hypothesized until the two diagnoses are dated independently and analgesic over-use is excluded.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at prospective-clinical-cohort, population-longitudinal-cohort, and dedicated-report class following the comorbidity-magnitude convention (the registered ocd, ptsd, abdominal-migraine, alice-in-wonderland-syndrome, cyclic-vomiting-syndrome, and occipital-neuralgia to migraine-headaches edges): the prospective clinical anchor is the only located design with a non-allergic subgroup and unexposed controls and reports migraine in 22.9 percent of that subgroup against 16.0 percent of controls with ICHD-3 ascertainment (PMID 41605462), the American Migraine Prevalence and Prevention anchor supplies the large-sample direction in a migraine-conditioned population with the mixed-rhinitis stratum carrying the adjusted significance (PMID 24275145), and the dedicated otorhinolaryngology report addresses the vasomotor-rhinitis and migraine pair directly at title level (PMID 33713559); because the quantitative subtype anchor is cross-sectional, the population anchor cannot establish direction and reports a null for its disability outcome after full adjustment, and the dedicated anchor carries no abstract, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with all three limits stated.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The only subtype-specific quantitative anchor is cross-sectional with 109 exposed participants and cannot establish temporal direction; the population anchor conditions on the migraine sample so direction between the conditions is not testable within it, and the significant adjusted result is carried by the mixed-rhinitis stratum rather than the non-allergic stratum; the same anchor's MIDAS disability association went null after full adjustment (OR 1.10, 95 percent CI 0.96-1.26), an explicit counterweight carried here; the dedicated vasomotor-rhinitis and migraine report carries no abstract in the PubMed record and supports only the existence of the association, not its magnitude; no located anchor adjusts for analgesic or NSAID over-use, a plausible confounder operating in the opposite direction.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Analgesic or NSAID over-use headache induced by self-medication for nasal symptoms
Allergic or mixed rhinitis misclassified as non-allergic rhinitis, the stratum carrying the population anchor's adjusted significance
Chronic rhinosinusitis or nasal polyposis as the coexisting upper-airway driver of headache
Sinus headache from pressure or ostiomeatal complex disease rather than migraine physiology

evidenceGaps: The only subtype-specific quantitative anchor is cross-sectional with 109 exposed participants and cannot establish temporal direction; the population anchor conditions on the migraine sample so direction between the conditions is not testable within it, and the significant adjusted result is carried by the mixed-rhinitis stratum rather than the non-allergic stratum; the same anchor's MIDAS disability association went null after full adjustment (OR 1.10, 95 percent CI 0.96-1.26), an explicit counterweight carried here; the dedicated vasomotor-rhinitis and migraine report carries no abstract in the PubMed record and supports only the existence of the association, not its magnitude; no located anchor adjusts for analgesic or NSAID over-use, a plausible confounder operating in the opposite direction.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because two independent designs quantify the co-occurrence with the non-allergic subtype specifically represented, and a dedicated report addresses the exact pair; the conservative framing carries the population anchor's null disability outcome, the mixed-rhinitis attribution, the absence of an abstract on the dedicated anchor, and the untested analgesic-over-use confounder, so the association is visible while direction and mechanism remain explicitly unasserted.

sourceReferences.citation: Yaka EC, Aghayarov ÖY, Değirmenci PB. The Association Between Rhinitis Subtypes and Migraine: A Comparative Clinical Study Clin Otolaryngol. 2026 May;51(3):449-457. PMID 41605462.
